gp.text:
For the three months ended September 30, 2026, gross profit decreased by $3.7 million, or 16.6%, to $18.6 million, as compared to $22.3 million for the same period in 2025. For the three months ended September 30, 2026, gross profit as a percentage of net sales decreased to 74.7%, as compared to 76.4% for the same period in 2025. The decrease in gross profit as a percentage of net sales was primarily due to increased freight and distribution costs, particularly in Hong Kong and Europe, as well as increased inventory reserve charges in the United States, Mexico, and Thailand, compared to the same period in 2025.

For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, gross profit decreased by $3.0 million, or 4.9%, to $57.9 million, as compared to $60.9 million for the same period in 2025. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, gross profit as a percentage of net sales increased to 75.8%, as compared to 74.8% for the same period in 2025. The increase in gross profit as a percentage of net sales was primarily due to more favorable pricing resulting in lower finished product costs, as compared to the same period in 2025. The timing of certain sales promotions also increased gross profit as a percentage of net sales during the nine months ended September 30, 2026, as compared to the same period in 2025.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Pension and retiree benefits
lines.why: Promised to employees for their work: operating (some analysts treat the unfunded part as debt).

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: Our business is not currently exposed to customer concentration risk given that no independent associate has ever accounted for more than 10% of our consolidated net sales.
For the year ended December 31, 2025, our operations outside of the Americas accounted for 69.9% of our consolidated net sales, as compared to 66.3% in 2024.

This decrease was primarily due to a 12.9% decline in the number of active independent associates and preferred customers and a 4.0% decrease in revenue per active independent associate and preferred customer.

In addition, net sales in the Asia/Pacific region was negatively impacted by a 13.9% decrease in the number of active independent associates and preferred customers, which was partially offset by a 17.0% increase in revenue per active independent associate and preferred customer.
We procure select products from single vendors who control certain product formulations, ingredients, or other intellectual property rights associated with such products.

Where available, we rely on common law trademark rights to protect our unregistered trademarks, even though such rights do not provide us with the same level of protection as afforded by a United States federal trademark registration.
To help ensure regulatory compliance, we rely on the advice of our outside legal counsel and regulatory consultants in each specific country.
We rely on our non-employee independent associates to market and sell our products to customers to generate growth and to attract new independent associates who are interested in building a business.
Our ability to increase sales depends on our ability to increase the number of customers in each of our markets around the world.
Our success will also depend on our ability to retain and motivate our existing independent associates and attract new independent associates.
We depend on the continued services of our executive officers and senior management team as they work closely with independent associate leaders and are responsible for our day-to-day operations.

Our ability to enter new markets and sustain satisfactory levels of sales in each market depends on the ability of our outside suppliers and manufacturers to provide required levels of ingredients and products and to comply with all applicable regulations.
However, the failure of our primary suppliers or manufacturers to supply ingredients or produce our products could adversely affect our business operations.
We depend on outside suppliers for raw materials.
We rely on our own systems and systems of third party vendors to assist our business.

Although we have implemented practices designed to maintain the availability of the information technology and service delivery systems we rely on and mitigate the harm of any unplanned interruptions, we cannot anticipate all eventualities.

We rely on internal systems and external systems maintained by manufacturers, distributors and service providers to take, fulfill and handle customer service requests and host certain online activities.
We rely upon our existing cash balances and cash flow from operations to fund our business and meet our contractual obligations.

Although our financial statements have been prepared on a going concern basis, this presentation depends on our ability to improve operating results, manage costs, and generate sufficient liquidity to meet our obligations as they become due.

As our primary source of liquidity has historically been from our cash flows from operations, this will be dependent on our ability to maintain and/or improve revenue as compared to operational expenses.
